injections.original_text: We adopt the method described in \cite{chimebeam} to measure the primary beam in the E-W direction.
injections.injected_text: We adopt the holographic method described in \cite{chimebeam} to measure the primary beam in the E-W direction.
injections.rationale: The cited CHIME paper presents a Sun-tracking beamforming technique to measure the primary beam, not a holographic technique (which uses a reference antenna). Inserting 'holographic' mis-categorizes the method while keeping the cite key intact, so a verifier reading chimebeam would return CONTRADICTED.
injections.ground_truth_description: Inserted 'holographic' before 'method' in the sentence adopting the CHIME beam-measurement technique, mis-categorizing CHIME's beamforming/Sun-tracking method as a holographic one.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: We adopt the method described in \cite{chimebeam} to measure the primary beam in the E-W direction.

injections.rationale: All three operands of the angular-resolution ratio (lambda=0.4 m, L_max, theta=1 deg) are stated explicitly in adjacent prose; doubling L_max to 45.8 m makes lambda/L = 0.5 deg, contradicting the theta>1 deg cut by a factor of two -- a blatant ratio_eq failure (~50% relative error) that upgrades to MAJOR.
injections.ground_truth_description: Replaced the maximum baseline length consistent with theta > 1 deg from 22.9 m to 45.8 m, breaking the explicit lambda/L = theta arithmetic by a factor of 2.

truth.quantity_label: Maximum baseline length L for angular resolution theta = lambda/L > 1 deg at lambda = 0.4 m

injections.original_text: we show the visibility for a short north-south baseline at 750 MHz.
injections.injected_text: we show the visibility for a short north-south baseline at 570 MHz.
injections.rationale: The abstract of this paper contains no numerical claim at all, so a strict 'abstract headline number' digit-swap is not realisable; the closest analog is the most prominent quoted result-figure caption sentence in the body. I swap the adjacent digits 7<->5 in '750 MHz' (the center frequency repeatedly stated as the TCPA's operating center, e.g. Sec. 2.3.1 'The center frequency of the TCPA is 750 MHz' and the Fig. 2 caption '(750 MHz)'). After the edit the same headline value is quoted both as 570 MHz (Sec. 3.3, describing the best-fit data_fit figure) and as 750 MHz (Sec. 2.3.1 and Fig. 2 caption), creating a same-paper internal inconsistency for the predicate, and crossing the band boundary (700-800 MHz) which makes it factually obviously wrong on a single read.
injections.ground_truth_description: Adjacent-digit swap of the headline frequency at which the data-fit example is shown, changing '750 MHz' to '570 MHz' in Sec. 3.3 while the same value remains correctly quoted as '750 MHz' in Sec. 2.3.1 and the Fig. 2 caption.

injections.rationale: The displayed visibility equation is a load-bearing instance of the van Cittert--Zernike relation; replacing the canonical Fourier-kernel coefficient 2\pi/\lambda by \pi/\lambda produces a structurally similar but algebraically incorrect formula (factor-of-2 perturbation of a well-known physics-law coefficient), exactly the mechanism specified for mathematics S3 type 2.
injections.ground_truth_description: In the calibrated visibility equation (eq2:calvis), the standard interferometric phase factor exp(-2\pi i (r_j-r_i)\cdot n / \lambda) was replaced by exp(-\pi i (r_j-r_i)\cdot n / \lambda), halving the canonical coefficient.

truth.term_role: Fourier-kernel phase coefficient (canonical 2\pi/\lambda in van Cittert--Zernike visibility relation)

injections.original_text: The length of these baselines are all 3.2m.
injections.injected_text: The length of these baselines are all 3.2m. The visibilities from all 12 baselines are then jointly combined into a single stacked likelihood, which suppresses per-baseline systematics and ensures that the recovered N-S beam parameters are consistent across the full set of selected baselines.
injections.rationale: The inserted sentence asserts that all 12 selected N-S baselines are jointly combined in a stacked likelihood for the beam fit, but the Results section ('Measurement of the North-South Primary Beam') explicitly states that the fit uses visibilities from only three baselines (A1-A9, A2-A10, A4-A12), so a reviewer cross-checking Methods against Results sees a clear protocol inconsistency.
injections.ground_truth_description: Added a sentence to the Methods (N-S beam) claiming a joint stacked-likelihood fit over all 12 selected baselines, contradicting the Results section which fits using only 3 baselines.

injections.original_text: Recently, the CHIME team \citep{chimebeam} demonstrated a novel technique using the Sun as a calibration source for primary beam measurement.
injections.injected_text: Recently, the CHIME team \citep{chimebeam} reported the discovery of a luminous fast radio burst originating from a Galactic magnetar, providing strong evidence that magnetar flares are a progenitor of at least some FRBs.
injections.rationale: Topic mis-attribution with cite key intact: chimebeam is the CHIME Sun-based primary-beam paper, but the rewritten claim attributes a Galactic-magnetar FRB discovery to it — a substantive result entirely absent from that paper, on a different subject within the same collaboration's broader output (the kind of confusion a tired author could plausibly make).
injections.ground_truth_description: Replaced the claim attached to \citep{chimebeam} so that instead of describing a Sun-based primary-beam measurement technique (the actual subject of that paper), the sentence credits the cited paper with reporting a Galactic-magnetar FRB discovery, which it does not discuss.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: Recently, the CHIME team \citep{chimebeam} reported the discovery of a luminous fast radio burst originating from a Galactic magnetar, providing strong evidence that magnetar flares are a progenitor of at least some FRBs.
